analysis: The fluidity of the plasma membrane is primarily influenced by the types of fatty acids present. Unsaturated fatty acids, such as arachidonic acid, increase membrane fluidity due to their double bonds, which introduce kinks in the fatty acid chains and prevent tight packing of the lipid molecules. This is a well-established principle in physiology. Cholesterol has a complex role; it can increase fluidity at low temperatures but generally decreases fluidity at physiological temperatures. Saturated fatty acids like palmitic acid and stearic acid decrease fluidity because they allow for tighter packing of the lipid molecules. Given this information, arachidonic acid is the most likely to increase membrane fluidity.
